Mean-field theory

Words: 44
Statistical physics OurBigBook.com
Mean-field theory replaces fluctuating interactions with a self-consistent average field. For example, an Ising spin feels a field determined by the average neighboring spin magnetization; a self-consistency equation approximates the interacting Ising model. Neglecting correlated fluctuations can fail near a continuous phase transition. The mean-field approximation in Landau theory is a particular use of this general framework.

Thermal fluctuation (⟨(δA)2⟩=kB​T∂h​⟨A⟩)

Words: 51
Statistical physics OurBigBook.com
A thermal fluctuation is the randomness of an observable in an equilibrium Boltzmann distribution. If the energy contains −hA, differentiation of its partition function gives ∂h​⟨A⟩=β(⟨A2⟩−⟨A⟩2). Thus the fluctuation variance is related to the response to a conjugate source. In a field theory, the two-point version is the connected correlation function.

Photon gas

Words: 77 Articles: 1
Statistical physics OurBigBook.com
A photon gas consists of photons in thermal equilibrium. Since photon number is not conserved when photons can be emitted and absorbed, the equilibrium photon chemical potential is zero. The photon energy density is aR​T4, where aR​=4σ/c, and its pressure is one third of this energy density.

Entropy density of a photon gas (s=4aR​T3/3)

Words: 38
Photon gas OurBigBook.com
For a photon gas, the first law of thermodynamics gives TdS=d(aR​T4V)+(aR​T4/3)dV, hence dS=(4aR​/3)d(T3V). Choosing zero entropy at zero temperature gives S=4aR​T3V/3. Adiabatic expansion with fixed relativistic species therefore preserves T3V; changing species or producing entropy requires a more general entropy balance.

Statistical mechanics

Words: 30
Statistical physics OurBigBook.com
Statistical mechanics connects microscopic states of a physical system to macroscopic thermal properties through probability distributions over those states. Its microcanonical ensemble, canonical ensemble and grand canonical ensemble encode different constraints on exchanges with the surroundings.

Ergodic hypothesis

Words: 88
Statistical physics OurBigBook.com
The ergodic hypothesis identifies long-time averages of equilibrium observables along typical trajectories with averages over the invariant equilibrium ensemble at the same conserved quantities. In the microcanonical formulation, the ensemble is normalized phase-space measure on the energy surface. In a measure-preserving description, ergodicity means invariant measurable sets have measure zero or one; the Birkhoff ergodic theorem then equates time averages and ensemble expectations almost everywhere for integrable observables. This explains why statistical-mechanical ensembles can predict long-time measurements. A particular mechanical model still requires its own ergodicity assumptions; integrable idealized systems need not be ergodic.

Latent heat of fusion (L)

Words: 23
Statistical physics OurBigBook.com
The latent heat of fusion is the energy per unit mass required to change a solid into a liquid at fixed phase-transition temperature.

Superfluidity

Words: 298 Articles: 6
Statistical physics OurBigBook.com
Superfluidity is a quantum-fluid response with phase stiffness and flow without viscous dissipation in an appropriate low-speed regime. A superfluid supports a phase-gradient current; defects and excitations can limit that flow. Bose-Einstein condensation concerns macroscopic one-particle occupation and is a distinct criterion: the Gaussian phase stiffness theory can have divergent absolute-phase fluctuations while retaining a cost for gradients.

Superfluid

Words: 248 Articles: 5
Superfluidity OurBigBook.com
A superfluid exhibits superfluidity, with phase stiffness and a phase-gradient current. In an appropriate ordered or quasi-ordered regime it supports low-speed flow without viscous dissipation, and its long-wavelength Goldstone boson has a sound-like dispersion. True thermodynamic phase selection and Bose-Einstein condensation need separate infrared conditions.

Normal component of a superfluid (vn​)

Words: 50
Superfluid OurBigBook.com
The normal component of a superfluid describes the momentum and entropy carried by excitations rather than the phase-gradient condensate current. Its velocity need not equal the superfluid velocity. In phenomenological condensate equations, prescribing its motion supplies a reference flow for dissipation; a full two-component fluid theory would also evolve its momentum and energy.

Superfluid velocity (u=(ℏ/m)∇S)

Words: 54
Superfluid OurBigBook.com
For a condensate ψ=n​eiS with kinetic operator −ℏ2∇2/(2m), its particle current is nu with the displayed velocity. This follows by subtracting the Gross–Pitaevskii equation from its complex conjugate. More generally, in units where the kinetic operator is −D∇2, the current velocity is 2D∇S. The complex argument gradient and current velocity coincide only when D=1/2.

Superfluid order-parameter effective theory

Words: 105 Articles: 2
Superfluid OurBigBook.com
For a complex superfluid order parameter ψ=n​eiθ, the nonrelativistic Landau-Ginzburg kinetic term contains −nθ˙. Thus number density and phase are canonically conjugate, so a phase-selected state necessarily fluctuates in particle number.
Number-phase conjugacy
Words: 31
Superfluid order-parameter effective theory OurBigBook.com
Number-phase conjugacy is the canonical relation between a conserved U(1) charge and the phase of its order parameter. A state of sharp number cannot also have a sharply selected broken-symmetry phase.
Thermal phase fluctuation
Words: 39
Superfluid order-parameter effective theory OurBigBook.com
A thermal phase fluctuation is a finite-temperature fluctuation of the phase of a complex order parameter. For a linearly dispersing phase mode, its infrared variance is proportional to T∫ddk/k2, which prevents true finite-temperature long-range order when d≤2.

Superconductivity

Words: 67 Articles: 1
Statistical physics OurBigBook.com
Superconductivity is a phase with vanishing electrical resistance and expulsion of magnetic flux from the bulk, the Meissner effect. Conventional microscopic BCS theory describes pairing of electrons into Cooper pairs.

Gauge-coupling sign in Ginzburg-Landau superconductivity (Dη​=∇−iηqA/ℏ)

Words: 42
Superconductivity OurBigBook.com
For energy with kinetic term ℏ2∣Dη​ψ∣2/(2m), η=±1, variation gives −ℏ2Dη2​ψ/(2m)+(α+β∣ψ∣2)ψ=0 and current j=ηqℏIm(ψ∗∇ψ)/m−q2∣ψ∣2A/m. Thus changing the sign of the covariant derivative changes the phase-gradient term of the current. The displayed energy, field equation and current must use the same convention.

Kinetic theory (f(t,x,v))

Words: 1k Articles: 23
Statistical physics OurBigBook.com
Describe many-particle systems through distributions on phase space. Transport moves particles along trajectories, while collision or diffusion terms modify their velocity distributions. The Boltzmann equation, Hamiltonian Liouville equation and Fokker-Planck equation are central models.

Boltzmann-Grad limit (Nad−1∼1,Nad→0)

Words: 62
Kinetic theory OurBigBook.com
For N hard particles in a fixed macroscopic volume, shrink their diameter a while keeping Nad−1 of order one. The occupied volume fraction tends to zero, but the mean free path stays macroscopic. Deriving the Boltzmann equation in this dilute limit requires control of recollisions and propagation of an incoming independence hypothesis related to molecular chaos for the Boltzmann equation. Its validity is not an automatic all-time consequence of small particle size.

Knudsen number (Kn=ℓmfp​/L)

Words: 47
Kinetic theory OurBigBook.com
The ratio of the mean free path to a macroscopic length compares collision and transport scales. Small Knudsen number motivates the hydrodynamic limit of the Boltzmann equation; large values favor a direct kinetic description. The scaling of time, velocity and space must also be stated when using it as a coefficient in a kinetic equation.

Molecular chaos for the Boltzmann equation

Words: 63
Kinetic theory OurBigBook.com
The incoming two-particle distribution at a collision is approximated by the product of one-particle distributions. This closes the binary collision term into the quadratic nonlinear Boltzmann collision operator. It does not assert exact independence after collisions: outgoing pairs can be correlated, and time reversal generally converts those correlations into incoming correlations. A rigorous kinetic limit needs propagation and convergence estimates rather than a bare independence assertion.

Unordered-pair collision rate (Γii​=Kii​Ni​(Ni​−1)/2)

Words: 51
Kinetic theory OurBigBook.com
For a dilute phase-mixed population, an identical-species collision rate counts unordered pairs: Γii​=Kii​Ni​(Ni​−1)/2. Different species have rate Γij​=Kij​Ni​Nj​. Here Kij​=⟨σij​vij​⟩/V uses the collision cross-section and relative speed. Destroying both identical particles gives N˙i​=−2Γii​, not −Γii​. This distinction prevents inconsistent factors when using one kinetic kernel for several particle sizes.

Kac model

Words: 449 Articles: 8
Kinetic theory OurBigBook.com
This many-particle stochastic collision model rotates one uniformly selected velocity pair by a uniformly selected angle, conserving the sum of squared velocities. Its normalized angular averaging is the Kac collision operator, and its continuous-time evolution is the Kac master equation. In this version velocities range over RN and initial energy is not restricted to one sphere; the evolution preserves the initial energy distribution.

Relative entropy in Kac's model (HN​(F)=∫Flog(F/γN​))

Words: 95 Articles: 1
Kac model OurBigBook.com
Use γN​=(2π)−N/2e−∣v∣2/2 as the reference probability density. The relative entropy is nonnegative by writing F=γN​u and integrating ulogu−u+1. Its expansion is ∫FlogF+(N/2)log(2π)+(1/2)∫∣v∣2F. Equality holds only at F=γN​, whereas other radial densities may still be stationary for the Kac master equation.
Kac entropy production (DN​(F)=−dtd​HN​(F)≥0)
Words: 53
Relative entropy in Kac's model OurBigBook.com
For the Kac master equation and finite differentiable entropy, mass and energy conservation remove the non-logarithmic entropy terms. Symmetrizing each pair rotation then gives DN​(F)=[2π(N−1)]−1∑i<j​∫∫(F∘Rij,θ​−F)log((F∘Rij,θ​)/F)dvdθ. The integrand is nonnegative by monotonicity of the logarithm, with the usual extended convention at zeros. Zero dissipation corresponds to radiality; it need not imply zero relative entropy.

Kac chaos (Πk​(FN​)⇀f⊗k)

Words: 64
Kac model OurBigBook.com
A permutation-symmetric sequence of probability laws is chaotic with one-particle law f when, for every fixed k, its k-coordinate marginal distributions converge weakly to the product law f⊗k as N→∞. This is an asymptotic independence condition, not a consequence of symmetry alone. A rigorous kinetic limit also requires propagation of this property under the dynamics and sufficient convergence to pass collision integrals.

Kac master equation (∂t​FN​=N(Q−I)FN​)

Words: 98 Articles: 1
Kac model OurBigBook.com
The jump process with total collision rate N and normalized pair-angle operator Q evolves by ∂t​FN​=N(Q−I)FN​. It preserves mass and the total squared velocity. Its one-coordinate distribution satisfies the Kac marginal evolution equation, and its Gaussian relative entropy in Kac's model decreases at the rate given by Kac entropy production.
Kac marginal evolution equation (∂t​Π1​=π−1∫(Π2​∘Rθ​−Π2​)dv2​dθ)
Words: 57
Kac master equation OurBigBook.com
For a permutation-symmetric density in the Kac master equation, integrate over all but the first velocity. Collisions among integrated coordinates cancel. The N−1 pairs containing the first coordinate give equal terms, with coefficient N(N−1)/(2π(2N​))=1/π. The resulting exact evolution depends on the two-coordinate marginal distribution; it is not a closed equation for the first marginal without additional asymptotic independence.

Kac collision operator (Q=(2N​)−1∑i<j​(2π)−1∫Uij,θ​dθ)

Words: 132 Articles: 2
Kac model OurBigBook.com
For N≥2, Uij,θ​F=F∘Rij,θ​ uses the genuine two-coordinate rotation (vi​,vj​)↦(vi​cosθ+vj​sinθ,−vi​sinθ+vj​cosθ). Average it uniformly over angles and pairs to obtain Q. Rotation invariance of Lebesgue measure makes Q a bounded self-adjoint operator of norm one on L2(RN). Each pair average is an orthogonal projection, but their full average is not in general a projection.
Dirichlet form of the Kac collision operator (⟨F,(I−Q)F⟩≥0)
Words: 80 Articles: 1
Kac collision operator OurBigBook.com
For the Kac collision operator, expanding the squared Hilbert space norm gives ⟨F,(I−Q)F⟩=(4π(2N​))−1∑i<j​∫02π​∫RN​∣F(Rij,θ​v)−F(v)∣2dvdθ. The nonnegative form measures failure of invariance under the pair rotations. It vanishes precisely on the radial kernel of the Kac collision operator.
Radial kernel of the Kac collision operator (ker(I−Q)=Lradial2​(RN))
Words: 51
Dirichlet form of the Kac collision operator OurBigBook.com
Zero Dirichlet form of the Kac collision operator forces invariance under every pair rotation; strong continuity upgrades almost every angle to every angle. Coordinate-plane rotations generate the special orthogonal group, whose action is transitive on each sphere for N≥2. Averaging over normalized Haar measure therefore identifies the invariant L2 functions with radial functions. Conversely radial functions are fixed by every pair rotation.

Free-transport phase mixing (f​t​(k,ξ)=f​0​(k,ξ+kt))

Words: 109 Articles: 1
Kinetic theory OurBigBook.com
On the unit-period spatial circle, free streaming has solution ft​(x,v)=f0​(x−tv,v). With Fourier phase e−2πi(kx+ξv), its mixed Fourier transform is f​t​(k,ξ)=f​0​(k,ξ+kt). A nonzero spatial mode of the velocity-integrated density therefore samples increasingly large velocity frequencies. The conserved spatial zero mode remains, while extra velocity regularity supplies quantitative decay of the other modes.

Uniform phase-mixing bound from velocity derivatives (∥ρt​−ρ∞​∥∞​≤2ζ(m)∥∂vm​f0​∥1​/(2π∣t∣)m)

Words: 53
Free-transport phase mixing OurBigBook.com
For m≥2 integrable weak velocity derivatives on a unit-period spatial circle, the Fourier transform of a derivative gives ∣f​0​(k,kt)∣≤∥∂vm​f0​∥1​/(2π∣kt∣)m for k=0. Summing these modes uses ∑k=0​∣k∣−m=2ζ(m). The resulting absolute Fourier summability gives the displayed uniform bound for the continuous representative of the density. For m=1 the same summation diverges, so this argument needs additional input.

Mean velocity of a kinetic distribution (u=∫f(x,v)dxdv∫vf(x,v)dxdv​)

Words: 41
Kinetic theory OurBigBook.com
The mass-normalized first velocity moment of a distribution on phase space. For a velocity-only distribution, omit the position integral. Nonzero finite mass and a finite first moment are required. For a probability distribution this is its expected value; its unnormalized counterpart is the momentum.

Hamiltonian Liouville equation (∂t​f+∇v​H⋅∇x​f−∇x​H⋅∇v​f=h)

A small column can result from a small local density, a small path length, or a small fraction of atoms in the absorbing state, so density inference requires these quantities to be constrained.

Electron number density (ne​)

Words: 24
Number density OurBigBook.com
Electron number density is the number of free electrons per unit volume. In fully ionized stellar matter, ne​=ρ/(μe​mu​), with mass density ρ and mean molecular weight per electron μe​.

Energy density (ρ)

Words: 21
Phase-space distribution function OurBigBook.com
The energy density is energy per unit volume. A homogeneous particle species with one-particle energy E(p) has
ρ=g∫(2π)3d3p​E(p)f(p).
(72)

Kinetic pressure of an isotropic gas

Words: 15
Phase-space distribution function OurBigBook.com
For an isotropic gas, averaging the momentum flux over directions gives
P=g∫(2π)3d3p​3E(p)p2​f(p).
(73)

Quantum magnetism

Words: 1k Articles: 29
Statistical physics OurBigBook.com
Quantum magnetism studies collective phases and excitations of interacting quantum spins.

Geometrical frustration

Words: 49
Quantum magnetism OurBigBook.com
Geometric frustration occurs when the interaction graph prevents all local preferred configurations from being satisfied simultaneously. Antiferromagnetic spins can be antiparallel on every bond of a bipartite graph, but three equal spins on a triangle instead minimize their total exchange by summing to zero, giving a coplanar 120-degree arrangement.

Hubbard model (H=Hhop​+UH​∑n​nn↑​nn↓​)

Words: 265 Articles: 5
Quantum magnetism OurBigBook.com
A lattice fermion model combining hopping with local density interaction, conventionally written UH​∑n​nn↑​nn↓​. Its interaction parameter must be matched when a spin-square representation is used: −2U(S2−3n/4) equals 3Un↑​n↓​, so UH​=3U for that representation.

On-site spin-square normal-ordering identity (:S2:=S2−3n/4=−3n↑​n↓​/2)

Words: 42
Hubbard model OurBigBook.com
For a single spinful fermion orbital, S2=3(n−2n↑​n↓​)/4. The contraction term is 3n/4, so :S2:=S2−3n/4=−3n↑​n↓​/2. Empty and doubly occupied states are spinless while singly occupied states have spin one half, which also proves the identity directly.

Itinerant ferromagnetism (ϵkσ​=ϵk​−σM)

Words: 185 Articles: 3
Hubbard model OurBigBook.com
Ferromagnetic spin polarization carried by mobile electrons rather than a separate fixed-spin lattice. A homogeneous spin field splits the electron bands and competes with a positive field cost. Mean-field instability is governed by the Stoner criterion; the ordered metal supports transverse spin waves as well as fermionic particle-hole excitations.
Mean-field itinerant ferromagnetic Goldstone mode (Eq​∼Dq2)
Words: 47
Itinerant ferromagnetism OurBigBook.com
An isotropic spin-polarized metal has a degenerate magnetization direction and a long-wavelength transverse magnon with quadratic dispersion. Nonzero spin density pairs the two transverse broken generators into one type-B Goldstone boson. Exchange-split Fermi surfaces also support fermionic low-energy excitations; the magnon is distinct from longitudinal amplitude motion and the spin-flip continuum.
Stoner criterion (Uc​χ0​=1,χ0​=∫ν(−nF′​)dϵ)
Words: 49
Itinerant ferromagnetism OurBigBook.com
In the homogeneous spin-vector mean-field scheme with field cost M2/(2U) and spin-summed density of states per site, the paramagnetic curvature is proportional to U−1−∫ν(ϵ)[−nF′​(ϵ)]dϵ. It changes sign at Uχ0​=1. For a smooth low-temperature density of states, χ0​≃ν(μ), giving the familiar Fermi-level criterion. Interaction and spin-counting conventions must be specified before comparing coefficients.
Homogeneous spin-field effective action (Seff​=βNM2/(2U)−∑kσ​ln[1+e−β(ϵk​−μ−σM)])
Words: 41
Itinerant ferromagnetism OurBigBook.com
Integrating free fermions in a constant auxiliary spin field gives Seff​=βNM2/(2U)−∑kσ​ln[1+e−β(ϵk​−μ−σM)]. Differentiation gives the self-consistent spin polarization. The extensive action is a mean-field restriction of the full auxiliary-field functional integral, not an exact omission of all spatial/time fluctuations.

Coordination number of a lattice (z)

Words: 35
Quantum magnetism OurBigBook.com
The coordination number z is the number of nearest neighbors of a lattice site. A Kac normalization divides a pair coupling by z so that the interaction energy per site remains finite as z→∞.

Néel state

Words: 169 Articles: 4
Quantum magnetism OurBigBook.com
A Néel state is a two-sublattice product state with antiparallel spin polarization on the two sublattices. It is the classical ordered reference state of a bipartite antiferromagnet.

Néel order parameter

Words: 142 Articles: 3
Néel state OurBigBook.com
The Néel order parameter is the slowly varying staggered magnetization of an antiferromagnet. On a bipartite lattice it changes sign between neighboring sublattices before coarse graining.
Quantum depletion of Néel order (Ms​=S−N−1∑k​vk2​)
Words: 63
Néel order parameter OurBigBook.com
For a linear spin-wave approximation, the ground state is empty of the diagonal quasiparticles but contains the original spin bosons. If ak​=uk​αk​−vk​α−k†​, their occupation number is vk2​. The staggered magnetization is reduced from S to S−N−1∑k​vk2​. For the one-dimensional nearest-neighbor Heisenberg antiferromagnet, vk2​=(∣sink∣−1−1)/2 and the integral diverges logarithmically. This invalidates finite ordered magnetization within the approximation; it is not itself a determination of the exact spectral gap.
Staggered magnetization
Words: 27
Néel order parameter OurBigBook.com
The staggered magnetization weights the local magnetization with opposite signs on the two sublattices of a bipartite graph. It is nonzero in a Néel state even when the uniform magnetization vanishes.
Uniform magnetization
Words: 26
Néel order parameter OurBigBook.com
The uniform magnetization is the nonalternating component of local spin polarization. In a nearly Néel-ordered antiferromagnet it describes the small canting shared by the two sublattices.

Long-range order

Words: 31
Quantum magnetism OurBigBook.com
Long-range order means that an appropriate connected or symmetry-resolved correlation remains nonzero at arbitrarily large separation. It cannot be created from a product state by a bounded-depth circuit of bounded-range gates.

Antiferromagnetic spin wave

Words: 113 Articles: 3
Quantum magnetism OurBigBook.com
An antiferromagnetic spin wave is a long-wavelength fluctuation of staggered magnetic order. In an isotropic ordered antiferromagnet its low-energy dispersion is linear.

Hypercubic antiferromagnetic spin-wave dispersion (ωk​=2dJS1−γk2​​)

Words: 44
Antiferromagnetic spin wave OurBigBook.com
For a nearest-neighbour Heisenberg antiferromagnet on a hypercubic lattice, the linear spin-wave approximation gives γk​=d−1∑j​cos(kj​a) and the displayed frequency. Near a gapless point its spin-wave velocity is 2JSad​. Its ground-state boson occupation is [1/1−γk2​​−1]/2, producing quantum depletion of Néel order. Exact zero modes need an infrared regulator or separate global-rotation treatment.

Spin-wave velocity (c)

Words: 23
Antiferromagnetic spin wave OurBigBook.com
The spin-wave velocity is the slope c=limk→0​ω(k)/k of a linearly dispersing spin wave. For the leading square-lattice Heisenberg antiferromagnet continuum theory, c=22​JSa.

Zeeman splitting

Words: 24
Antiferromagnetic spin wave OurBigBook.com
Zeeman splitting is the separation of energy levels or mode frequencies by a background magnetic field. Opposite circular spin polarizations receive opposite frequency shifts.

Ferromagnetic spin chain

Words: 168 Articles: 5
Quantum magnetism OurBigBook.com
A ferromagnetic spin chain favors aligned neighbouring spins. Its conventional long-wavelength magnons have quadratic dispersion.

Easy-plane anisotropy

Words: 20
Ferromagnetic spin chain OurBigBook.com
Easy-plane anisotropy penalizes spin components normal to a preferred plane, leaving a low-energy angular degree of freedom within that plane.

Ferromagnetic magnon

Words: 133 Articles: 3
Ferromagnetic spin chain OurBigBook.com
A ferromagnetic magnon is a quantized spin wave. Without a linear restoring term its long-wavelength frequency is proportional to k2.
Nearest-neighbour ferromagnetic magnon dispersion (Ek​=4JSsin2(k/2))
Words: 80 Articles: 1
Ferromagnetic magnon OurBigBook.com
For H=−J∑n​Sn​⋅Sn+1​ and unit spacing, the one-magnon energy is 2JS(1−cosk)=4JSsin2(k/2). The exact one-magnon hopping matrix has diagonal 2JS and neighbour entries −JS. The same result follows from the linear spin-wave approximation. Its long-wavelength stiffness is JS, with energy proportional to k2.
Next-nearest-neighbour ferromagnetic magnon dispersion (Ek​=4S[J1​sin2(k/2)+J2​sin2k])
Words: 34
Nearest-neighbour ferromagnetic magnon dispersion OurBigBook.com
Positive nearest- and next-nearest-neighbour exchanges give one-magnon energy 2S[J1​(1−cosk)+J2​(1−cos2k)]. At small momentum this is S(J1​+4J2​)k2. The quadratic-boson result describes the harmonic many-magnon spectrum; higher-order spin-wave interactions remain in the full Hamiltonian.
Damped ferromagnetic spin wave
Words: 32
Ferromagnetic magnon OurBigBook.com
A damped ferromagnetic spin wave has a complex pole ω=±ωk​−iΓk​. Both poles of its retarded Green function must lie in the lower half of the complex frequency plane so that the response respects causality.

Spin coherent-state Berry phase

Words: 160 Articles: 4
Quantum magnetism OurBigBook.com
The spin coherent-state path integral contains a Berry phase equal, modulo gauge choices, to the spin S times the solid angle swept on the Bloch sphere. Single-valued path-integral amplitudes require 2S∈Z.

Wess–Zumino term

Words: 65 Articles: 1
Spin coherent-state Berry phase OurBigBook.com
For a spin coherent-state history, a Wess--Zumino term records the oriented target-sphere area bounded by the spin path. Its variation is local even though a single gauge-patch expression for the area need not be global.
Antiferromagnetic Wess–Zumino term
Words: 30
Wess–Zumino term OurBigBook.com
In a bipartite antiferromagnet, the smooth staggered contributions to the spin Wess--Zumino terms cancel between sublattices. Their term linear in uniform canting is proportional to m⋅(n×∂t​n).

CP1 spinor representation (CP1 spinor representation)

Words: 62 Articles: 1
Spin coherent-state Berry phase OurBigBook.com
The CP1 spinor representation writes a unit vector as ni​=z†σi​z with z†z=1. The phase redundancy z↦eiαz identifies normalized spinors that represent the same point of the two-sphere.
Ferromagnetic Wess–Zumino term
Words: 31
CP1 spinor representation OurBigBook.com
The ferromagnetic Wess–Zumino term is the first-order kinetic term iκz†z˙ in the CP1 description. A local phase change of z changes it only by the total derivative −κα˙.

Fermi liquid

Words: 437 Articles: 11
Statistical physics OurBigBook.com
A Fermi liquid is an interacting fermion phase whose low-energy excitations are long-lived quasiparticles near a Fermi surface. Its effective interactions are classified by scaling only the frequency and momentum normal to that surface.

Fermi surface

Words: 20
Fermi liquid OurBigBook.com
A Fermi surface is the codimension-one surface in momentum space separating occupied and unoccupied zero-temperature states of a fermionic system.

Fermi-surface renormalization-group scaling

Words: 32
Fermi liquid OurBigBook.com
Fermi-surface renormalization-group scaling sends frequency and normal displacement from the Fermi surface to zero while leaving tangential momentum fixed. Generic interactions are irrelevant, while forward-scattering and opposite-momentum Cooper channels can remain marginal.

BCS theory

Words: 352 Articles: 8
Fermi liquid OurBigBook.com
BCS theory describes a superconducting instability caused by attractive interactions between opposite-momentum fermions near a Fermi surface.

Cooper pair

Words: 42
BCS theory OurBigBook.com
A Cooper pair is a correlated pair of fermions associated with superconductivity. The conventional BCS ground state uses opposite-momentum, opposite-spin pair creation operators ck↑†​c−k↓†​. Their total momentum is zero for every relative momentum k; zero total momentum does not restrict k to zero.

BCS ground state (∏k​(uk​+vk​ck↑†​c−k↓†​)∣0⟩)

Words: 56
BCS theory OurBigBook.com
The BCS ground state is the normalized product of empty and occupied pair states ∏k​(uk​+vk​bk†​)∣0⟩. For uk2​+vk2​=1, each pair factor is normalized. The inverse Bogoliubov transformation annihilates it, so it is the vacuum of positive-energy quasiparticles. Although individual factors use opposite momenta, k runs over the relative pair momenta; it is not restricted to k=0.

BCS coherence factors (uk2​+vk2​=1)

Words: 42
BCS theory OurBigBook.com
For real gap and the particle-hole block (ξk​−Δk​​−Δk​−ξk​​), the BCS coherence factors obey uk2​=(1+ξk​/Ek​)/2, vk2​=(1−ξk​/Ek​)/2 and uk​vk​=Δk​/(2Ek​), where Ek​=ξk2​+Δk2​​. They diagonalize the Bogoliubov--de Gennes Hamiltonian and give the empty/pair amplitudes of the BCS ground state. Their relative sign depends on the pairing convention.

BCS anomalous average (⟨c−k↓​ck↑​⟩)

Words: 38
BCS theory OurBigBook.com
The BCS anomalous average is the pair expectation ⟨bk​⟩=⟨c−k↓​ck↑​⟩. In the BCS ground state it is uk​vk​=Δk​/(2Ek​) for real gap at zero temperature. At temperature T it becomes Δk​tanh(Ek​/(2kB​T))/(2Ek​). Substitution into the pairing-field definition gives the BCS gap equation.

Reduced BCS pairing Hamiltonian

Words: 36
BCS theory OurBigBook.com
The reduced BCS pairing Hamiltonian retains scattering of opposite-momentum, opposite-spin Cooper pairs:
H=∑k,σ​ϵk​ckσ†​ckσ​+∑k,k′​Vk,k′​bk†​bk′​,bk†​=ck↑†​c−k↓†​.
(74)
A mean-field approximation introduces the BCS anomalous average and pairing field Δk​=−∑k′​Vk,k′​⟨bk′​⟩. The subtraction −∑Vk,k′​⟨bk†​⟩⟨bk′​⟩ corrects the double counting of the mean-field interaction energy.

Cooper instability

Words: 37
BCS theory OurBigBook.com
The Cooper instability is the logarithmic growth of an attractive BCS coupling at low energy. If νF​ is the density of states and V<0, perturbation theory breaks down at a scale proportional to Λe−1/(νF​∣V∣).

BCS gap equation

Words: 85 Articles: 1
BCS theory OurBigBook.com
At zero temperature and weak coupling, the BCS gap equation gives Δ≃2Λe−1/(νF​∣V∣). Its exponential scale agrees with the renormalization-group scale of the Cooper instability.
Constant-shell BCS gap equation (Δ=ΩD​/sinh(1/(νs​V)))
Words: 60
BCS gap equation OurBigBook.com
An attractive interaction Vk,k′​=−V/V within ∣ξk​∣,∣ξk′​∣<ΩD​ gives a constant gap inside that energy shell and zero outside. With approximately constant single-spin density of states νs​ per volume,
1=νs​V∫0ΩD​​ξ2+Δ2​dξ​=νs​Varsinh(ΩD​/Δ),Δ=sinh(1/(νs​V))ΩD​​.
(75)
The weak coupling limit is Δ≃2ΩD​e−1/(νs​V). A density counting both spin species is twice νs​ and must be divided by two. The shell cutoff is a relative-energy condition, even when every Cooper pair has zero total momentum.

Coulomb collision

Words: 33
Statistical physics OurBigBook.com
A Coulomb collision is the deflection or energy exchange of charged particles through their electric interaction. In a dilute plasma, the cumulative effect of many small-angle encounters controls transport and interspecies thermal equilibration.
